title: Describe safety and traffic control procedures
intro: Traffic control is a planned system for road users, workers and equipment. Signs, devices, traffic control persons (TCPs), traffic assistants and communication have defined roles. A paving learner must understand that system even when they are not assigned to control traffic. At a community entrance, include pedestrians, cyclists, mobility needs and emergency access in the planning questions.

sections.title: Describe traffic control procedures (TCP) Certification
sections.text:
WorkSafeBC Part 18 defines traffic-control training and responsibilities. Section 18.6.2 addresses a traffic-control-person training program, including knowledge and practical competency assessment; the employer must meet the applicable qualification requirements. A classroom paving chapter does not issue that qualification. Confirm the accepted training program and the actual person’s current evidence before assigning TCP duties.

A traffic assistant has a different role and workplace training requirements under 18.6.3. Do not relabel an unqualified person a TCP because the crew needs help. Course completion records, employer orientation and site-specific instruction serve different purposes; all applicable requirements must be met.

sections.title: Review TCP training content
sections.text:
Traffic-control training develops recognition of hazards, the required plan, setup and removal of devices, safe positioning and escape routes, signs/signals, communication and responses to changing conditions. The B.C. Traffic Management Manual for Work on Roadways provides the roadwork framework, used with current regulation and road-authority requirements.

The learner reads the approved plan’s location, revision, work activity and traffic arrangement before interpreting an individual sign. A diagram from a manual is a typical arrangement with conditions, not a ready-made plan for every site. Conditions such as sight distance, road speed, intersections, queues, pedestrians and lighting affect the actual plan.

sections.title: Review TCP regulations
sections.text:
The number and positioning of people and devices follow the risk assessment, applicable requirements and approved traffic-control arrangement. There is no universal answer of one or two TCPs for all paving work. Under 18.8, the position must be identified as safe in the risk assessment; escape and approach visibility matter. Equipment is kept clean and serviceable. Precise, deliberate signals and effective communication between multiple TCPs are required by the relevant provisions.

The paver crew must not change the traffic arrangement informally when production slows or a truck arrives. Communicate the changing need to the responsible person, maintain the controls and wait for an authorized adjustment. A queue extending beyond the planned warning arrangement is a changed condition requiring action, not a reason to hurry signals.

worked.title: The plan revision matters
worked.case: Fictional documents: T-02 revision A places the facility entrance outside the work area. Revision B extends the work beyond that entrance. The crew has B, but a traffic briefing still uses A.
worked.solution: The drawings describe different access conditions. Before work under the changed arrangement, resolve the mismatch through the responsible traffic-control planner/supervisor and brief all affected roles. Record the current approved revision and the entrance provisions. An extra cone added by an unassigned person does not resolve the plan conflict.

activities.prompt: Compare TCP and traffic-assistant training requirements using retained Part 18 sections 18.6.2–18.6.3. Identify what qualification this chapter does not issue.
activities.answer: TCP training includes the specified program and knowledge/practical assessment; traffic assistants have workplace training addressing their defined tasks. Neither role is conferred by this reading.
activities.title: Explain and apply the idea

activities.prompt: Annotate the work-zone concept with questions about warning, transition, work area, public route and return to normal traffic. Explain why no spacing can be taken from it.
activities.answer: Concept identifies functions, not actual distances or approval. Obtain the road-authority plan/risk assessment and current requirements; address visibility, queues and vulnerable road users.
activities.title: Calculate and check the result

activities.prompt: Save a version register for the worked case, then role-play a revision handover. Ask the listener to find the current entrance instruction and improve the brief if they cannot.
activities.answer: Register retains A as superseded and B as current only when confirmed by the authorized system. The handover identifies affected people and the changed access provision; digital and individual feedback evidence are retained.

practical: Check the actual site plan and role qualifications before road-side observation.
Observe correct interpretation, staying within assigned duties and communication of a changed condition.
Where TCP competence is assessed, use the approved training/assessment program and qualified assessor, not this classroom record alone.
